notes: Fixes the stuck-cancelling bug at its root: expanded callers, including nested ones, now derive their status from their children through RefreshReusableCallerStatus instead of being written as cancelled directly, and cancelRun now calls EmitJobsIfReadyByRun when a settled run has no job left to emit, which frees the concurrency group. Weak spots: an extra DB reload per caller, a 'changed' check against the stale in-memory status, and a reliance on ID-descending order that matches the comment only when children have higher IDs than their callers. Tests are good: a nested-caller test covers cancel, runner ack and run status, and a mocked emit test covers force-cancel.

Fixes the root cause. Callers at any nesting level are now settled deepest-first by recomputing their status from their children rather than being written as cancelled, and `cancelRun` re-emits the run's concurrency check when a cancel only settles an already-finished run. The `len(updatedJobs)==0` guard depends on emission happening elsewhere for other paths, and the function-variable swap is a little clever, but the change is focused and both bugs have targeted tests (nested callers with runner ack, and force-cancel emission via a mock).

Walks the checked CEL AST at provision time to collect literal `ph()` placeholder names, flagging non-literal names as dynamic. It then retries on a response only when an expression reads status, header or latency placeholders. This covers the shorthand and direct `ph()` forms, escaped literals, lookalike names and dynamic names, with thorough unit tests and an end-to-end POST passthrough test.

Fixes the root cause by walking the checked CEL AST at provision time to collect the literal names passed to `ph()`, with a conservative dynamic-name flag. Only expressions that read status_code/status_text/header.*/latency placeholders are evaluated against the response. Escaped and string-literal look-alikes, `status_codes`, `upstream.host`, direct `ph()` calls and computed names all behave as the maintainers specified. It adds a small exported method on MatchExpression, which is a justified API addition. Thorough table tests plus an end-to-end passthrough test cover the cases.

Adds `--links` support to both zip and squashfs: symlinks are skipped with a notice naming the flag, listed with the `.rclonelink` suffix, sized by target length, opened with range/seek honoured, and checked for clashes so `NewObject` agrees with listing; it handles the hostile archive by dropping any symlink that has members inside it. Drawbacks: zip reads every symlink target eagerly at open time, which is costly on remote backends; squashfs only checks clashes against `name.rclonelink`, not a same-named dir; and one hidden test fails, likely over the expected hostile-archive or squashfs behaviour.

Implements --links gating with a notice, `.rclonelink` naming, target-length size, range/seek-aware reads and List/NewObject consistency for both zip and squashfs, and blocks the hostile-archive escape by dropping any symlink that clashes with another entry; however, zip eagerly opens every symlink at listing time (extra range reads on S3), `addLinks` pokes directly into DirTree's map internals, one hidden test fails, and the case-insensitive-destination escape is not addressed.

The core fix matches the maintainer notes: `Close()` is added to the interface, `Get`/`Walk` reconnect a closed connection first, `Reconnect` clears the USM engine ID, boots, time, localized keys and context engine ID before `Connect()`, and `Gather` closes the agent connection on any field or table error. Its weak points are that it writes the USM fields without gosnmp's lock and edits the unrelated `TestSnmpInitGosmi` (relative path plus Log). The added tests are otherwise thorough, but the package suite fails, which suggests one of the new or edited tests is broken or fragile.

Fixes the root cause as the maintainers asked: Close() is added to the Connection interface, Get/Walk reconnect a closed connection first, Reconnect clears the discovered USM engine ID/boots/time, localized keys and ContextEngineID only when the connection is closed, and Gather closes an agent's connection after any field or table failure; the new tests are solid, but the patch also rewrites the unrelated TestSnmpInitGosmi (path handling, logger) as an environment workaround, and the package suite still fails.

The design looks sound and fixes the root cause: one shared ref-counted state keeps its own dup'd fd and the real path, then unlinks and closes both under the mutex when the last holder releases; double-close guards, the close/listen race and abstract sockets are also handled. However, all 7 hidden tests fail and the package suite does not pass, most likely a compile conflict with the reworked internal types or test helpers, so it cannot be credited as working.

Reading the code, the fix looks sound: a shared ref-counted socket keeps its own dup'd fd, the leaked File() dups are gone, the real path is unlinked on last release, double close is guarded by a CAS and returns net.ErrClosed, a racing listen is safe, and abstract sockets are never unlinked. But all 7 hidden tests and the package suite fail, likely because the rewrite changed internals the tests rely on (the unixSockets map type, the unixListener fields, deleteListener becoming a pointer, and release() always taking unixSocketsMu), so its correctness is unproven against the real tests.

Fixes both sides of the bug and passes the hidden tests: a `DiffPathPrefixes()` helper forces `noprefix`/`mnemonicPrefix`/`srcPrefix`/`dstPrefix` on every diff lazygit reads back, and the parser now strips any single-component prefix, handles the `rename to`/`copy to` fallback and keeps `/dev/null`. The tradeoff is that users who set `mnemonicPrefix` now see `a/`/`b/` in the lazygit diff view, and the truncated diff hides the `diff --git` splitting logic and any parser tests, so beyond the updated command-arg expectations the test coverage can't be verified.

Adds a `DiffPathPrefixes()` builder helper that forces `a/` and `b/` prefixes on every diff lazygit requests (including worktree and stash diffs that had no prefix override before), strips any single prefix component in the parser, keeps `/dev/null` as is, and reads `rename to`/`copy to` lines. All hidden tests pass, but forcing `mnemonicPrefix=false` on displayed diffs silently overrides the user's display preference, the truncated `diff --git` splitting can't be fully verified, and the visible test changes are only mechanical arg-list updates.

The approach is plausible: it tracks the max exemplar timestamp per memSeries, keeps empty series in gc/gcSeries while the exemplar is at or after minValidTime, releases chunks for selected/stale compaction, and observes exemplars on commit, WAL replay and snapshot load. However, it changes the internal gc/gcSeries signatures, adds 8 bytes to every memSeries, narrows the pending-commit mask, and its tests use the `new(expr)` syntax, which may not compile on the repo's Go version; it fails all hidden tests and the package suite.

The design is sound: it tracks each series' max exemplar timestamp on commit, WAL replay and snapshot replay. It keeps the series in `gc`/`gcSeries` while that timestamp is at or after `minValidTime`, and releases the chunks of retained series. However, all hidden tests fail and the package suite fails, most likely a compile break from the changed internal `gc`/`gcSeries` signatures and/or the Go-1.26-only `new(int64(...))` syntax in its tests. It also adds 8 bytes to every `memSeries` and shrinks the pending-commit counter to 29 bits.
